_note: Explanations for gaps between the primary value and a second source (tools/validate.mjs). Each note is shown in the app next to the value as 'Other sources'. Numbers quoted here are the values in data/crosscheck.json.
He:mp: PubChem's 0.95 K is not a 1-atm melting point: at 1 atm helium has no solid phase (no melting point in CRC via mendeleev, none in the Wikipedia infobox). The sample view uses 'no solid at 1 atm'.
C:mp: Carbon does not melt at 1 atm: it sublimes (Wikipedia infobox 3915 K; CRC via mendeleev 4098 K). PubChem's 3823 K is kept with this note; the sample view uses sublimation.
Ga:bp: Handbooks differ: PubChem 2477 K, CRC (mendeleev) 2502 K. The Wikipedia infobox gives 2676 K from Zhang, Evans & Zhang (2011), 'Corrected values for boiling points and enthalpies of vaporization of elements in handbooks', J. Chem. Eng. Data 56, doi:10.1021/je1011086. Unresolved: QUESTIONS.md Q10.
Cs:density: PubChem 1.93 g/cm³; Wikipedia (Arblaster 2018, 20 °C) 1.886 and CRC (mendeleev) 1.873 g/cm³. The two handbook values agree within 0.7 %; PubChem is 2–3 % higher. QUESTIONS.md Q10.
Ba:bp: PubChem 2170 K; Wikipedia and CRC (mendeleev) both give 2118 K. QUESTIONS.md Q10.
